Fake IRS scams
How to spot one

lines.text: That IRS call demanding gift cards? It's a scam. Every time.
lines.say: That IRS call demanding gift cards? It's a scam. Every time.

lines.text: Americans reported losing about $15.9 billion to fraud in 2025, up from about $8.8 billion in 2022, per the FTC.
lines.say: Americans reported losing about fifteen point nine billion dollars to fraud in 2025, up from about eight point eight billion in 2022, per the FTC.

lines.text: By our math, that's about 81% more in three years.
lines.say: By our math, that's about eighty-one percent more in three years.

lines.text: Imposters, like fake government agents, took about $3.5 billion of that in 2025.
lines.say: Imposters, like fake government agents, took about three point five billion dollars of that in 2025.

lines.text: Here's the tell: the IRS says it normally contacts you first with a letter in the mail.
lines.say: Here's the tell: the IRS says it normally contacts you first with a letter in the mail.

lines.text: It won't demand gift cards, crypto or a wire, threaten arrest, or text you first about a bill.
lines.say: It won't demand gift cards, crypto or a wire, threaten arrest, or text you first about a bill.

lines.text: Fake IRS texts, emails and AI robocalls made the IRS Dirty Dozen scam list in 2026.
lines.say: Fake IRS texts, emails and A I robocalls made the IRS Dirty Dozen scam list in 2026.

lines.text: To check, log in at IRS.gov or call the number on your notice. Send fakes to phishing@irs.gov, and forward texts to 7726.
lines.say: To check, log in at IRS dot gov or call the number on your notice. Send fakes to phishing at IRS dot gov, and forward texts to seven seven two six.

lines.text: So hang up, then look it up yourself.
lines.say: So hang up, then look it up yourself.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: The IRS Never Asks for Gift Cards: Spot the Fake Call
post.ig:
That IRS call demanding gift cards? It's a scam. Every time.
Americans reported losing about $15.9 billion to fraud in 2025, up from $8.8 billion in 2022 (FTC).
Imposter scams took about $3.5 billion in 2025.
The real IRS normally contacts you first by mail, and never demands gift cards, crypto or wire transfers.
Verify at IRS.gov or the number on your notice. Report to phishing@irs.gov, forward texts to 7726.
Sources: IRS, FTC Consumer Sentinel, IRS Dirty Dozen 2026.
News and education, not financial advice.
